summary: George Santayana was a philosopher who studied at Boston Latin School, Harvard, Berlin, and Cambridge, completing his PhD at Harvard under William James. He served on Harvard's philosophy faculty from 1907 to 1912.

George Scott Robertson worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. After studying at Westminster Hospital, he joined the Indian Medical Service in 1878 and the Foreign and Political Department in 1888.

George Sherman Lane worked in linguistics and Indology, earning degrees at Iowa and Chicago. After studying in Iceland and Paris, he taught at Chicago, Catholic University of America, and the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (1937–1972).

George Shirt was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the Church Missionary Society College, Islington, and the University of Cambridge, serving as a missionary with the Church Mission Society from 1866 and as a fellow at Mumbai.

George Smith worked in history, archaeology, and Indology, earning an LL.D. from the University of Edinburgh. He served as a professor at Doveton College in 1854 and as a fellow at the University of Calcutta from 1856 to 1875.

George Speirs Alexander Ranking worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology. Educated at Aldenham School and St Catharine's College, Cambridge, he served as University Lecturer in Persian at Balliol College, Oxford, and Professor of Persian at Calcutta.

George Thibaut worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Heidelberg and Berlin under Albrecht Weber and Adolf Holtzmann, later holding principalships at Benares, Muir Central College, and Sanskrit College, and a professorship at the University of Calcutta.

George Thompson was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at the University of California, Berkeley, under Frits Staal and Martin Schwartz. His career included appointments at Illinois, UCLA, Catholic University of Louvain, and the University of Haifa.
George Turnbull Marshall was an Indologist. He served as Secretary at Fort William College from 1838 to 1852 and as Secretary at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University from 1839 to 1840.
George Turnour was an Indologist and historian who contributed to Buddhist studies. He served in the Ceylon Civil Service starting in 1818, becoming Assistant to the Commissioner of Revenue in 1820.

George Uglow Pope worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as head of Breeks Memorial School and Bishop Cotton Boys' School, a fellow of the University of Madras, and Lecturer in Tamil at the University of Oxford from 1883.

George V. Bobrinskoy was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Lutheran Theological Seminary, Pennsylvania, and Yale under Franklin Edgerton. He taught Sanskrit at Yale (1927–1928) before a long career at the University of Chicago (1928–1967).

George Watt worked in Indology and other fields. Educated at Aberdeen, Glasgow, and King's College London, he held professorships of botany at Calcutta and Presidency University, curated at the Indian Museum, and lectured at Edinburgh.

George Weston Briggs was an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at Northwestern. He taught at Lucknow Christian College, University of the Pacific, and Goucher College, and served as professor at Drew University from 1925 to 1944.

George William Brown specialized in Indology and religious studies, earning his PhD at Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield. He held posts at Christian Bible College, the College of Missions, and Lexington Theological Seminary.

George de Roerich worked in Tibetology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at London, Harvard, and Paris, he directed the Urusvati Institute and later held positions at Kalimpong College, Moscow State University, and Chicago.

George van Driem is a linguist and Tibetologist who studied at Virginia, Nijmegen, and Leiden. He held the Chair for Descriptive Linguistics at Leiden (1996–2009) and the Chair of Historical Linguistics at Bern (2010–2022).

Georges B. J. Dreyfus specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at several Tibetan monasteries, the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, and the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, later becoming Jackson Professor of Religion at Williams College.

Georges Cuendet worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Geneva, Basel, EPHE, and INALCO under Charles Bally and Antoine Meillet. He taught at Gymnase de Nyon, the University of Geneva (1938–1963), and the University of Lausanne.

Georges Dandoy was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Namur, Stonyhurst, Oxford, and St. Mary's College, Kurseong, and held posts at St. Xavier's College in Mumbai, St. Mary's, and the University of Calcutta.
